children.note: Every bit of state power is the people's — Kenyans own it — and may only be used the way this Constitution allows. The people use it themselves (for example in a referendum) or through the leaders they elect.

children.topic: Clause 1: power belongs to the people
children.note: All sovereign power is the people's, and it may be exercised only as the Constitution says.

manas.q: Who holds sovereign power in Kenya, and on what condition?

children.note: The people act directly (a referendum, a petition) or through the representatives they elect democratically.

children.topic: Clause 3: delegated to three kinds of State organ
children.note: The people lend their power to Parliament and the county assemblies, the national and county executives, and the Judiciary and independent tribunals. Each must act within the Constitution.

manas.q: To which State organs is sovereign power delegated?

children.note: Parliament (National Assembly and Senate) and the 47 county assemblies make law.
The national executive (President, Cabinet) and the county executives (governors) carry out the law.
Courts and independent tribunals decide disputes and check the other two.
Sovereign power is exercised at the national level and at the county level.

manas.q: At which two levels is sovereign power exercised?

children.note: The Constitution is the highest law and binds every person and every State organ at both levels of government. Anything that clashes with it is void, as far as the clash goes.
The Constitution sits above all other law and binds every person and every State organ, national and county.

children.topic: Clause 2: no State authority outside it
children.note: Nobody may claim or use State authority unless the Constitution authorises it.

children.topic: Clause 3: cannot be challenged in court
children.note: No court or State organ may question whether the Constitution itself is valid or legal.
A law of any kind, customary law included, that contradicts the Constitution is void as far as the contradiction goes; an act done against the Constitution is invalid.

manas.q: What happens to a law that conflicts with the Constitution?

children.note: Only the clashing part dies; the rest of the Act survives. Courts usually sever the bad section.
A custom (for example on inheritance) that discriminates contrary to Article 27 is void on that point.
A county by-law that bans all demonstrations would clash with Article 37 and be void to that extent.
The general rules of international law are part of Kenyan law.

children.topic: Clause 6: ratified treaties are Kenyan law
children.note: A treaty or convention that Kenya has ratified becomes Kenyan law by force of the Constitution itself.

manas.q: When does a treaty become part of Kenyan law?

children.note: Everyone has a duty to respect, uphold and defend the Constitution. Trying to set up a government in any other way than the Constitution allows is unlawful.

children.topic: Clause 1: a duty on every person
children.note: Respecting, upholding and defending the Constitution is an obligation of every person, not only officials.

manas.q: Who has the duty to defend the Constitution?

children.note: Any attempt to establish a government outside the Constitution (for example a coup) is unlawful.
Kenyan decisions read on Kenya Law (new.kenyalaw.org) that turned on this chapter. One line each; open the link for the judgment.

children.topic: AG v Ndii (BBI case), Supreme Court 2022
children.note: The Supreme Court held that the "basic structure" doctrine (an unamendable core) does not apply in Kenya, and that the President cannot start a constitutional amendment through the popular-initiative route. The Constitution of Kenya (Amendment) Bill 2020 was therefore unconstitutional. Shows how Article 1 sovereignty is exercised only through the Constitution's own amendment rules (Chapter 16).
